bib.title: Learning multiple visual domains with residual adapters

question: How can one ResNet represent ten very different visual domains with most parameters shared, without forgetting earlier domains?
hypothesis: Small domain-specific residual 1x1-conv adapters (plus BN) on a shared, frozen ResNet can match or beat full fine-tuning per domain at a fraction of the parameters.
contributions: A residual adapter module design for multiple-domain learning (section 3)
The Visual Decathlon benchmark and score (section 4)

method.summary: Insert domain-specific residual adapter modules g(x;a)=x+a*x (1x1 filters, with BN) into a ResNet28 pre-trained on ImageNet, freeze the shared weights and train only adapters/BN per new domain. Compared with scratch, frozen features, fine-tuning, LwF and BN-only adaptation on ten datasets.

datasets.name: Visual Decathlon: ImageNet ILSVRC12, Aircraft, CIFAR-100, Daimler Pedestrian, DTD, GTSR, VGG-Flowers, Omniglot, SVHN, UCF101 (dynamic images)
datasets.size: ImNet 1.3m, Aircraft 7k, C100 50k, DPed 30k, DTD 4k, GTSR 40k, Flowers 2k, OGlt 26k, SVHN 70k, UCF 9k images (Table 1 header, training sizes)
datasets.split: original splits where they exist; else 60/20/20 train/val/test; ImageNet validation used as test, new validation sampled from train
datasets.source: ten public datasets; no external data allowed
datasets.preprocessing: images resized isotropically to shorter side 72 px; network input 64x64; UCF101 videos converted with Dynamic Image encoding

models.name: ResNet28 (wide ResNet style)
models.architecture: three blocks of four residual units, 3x3 conv-BN-ReLU, global average pooling, softmax classifier

models.name: Residual adapters
models.params: about 11% extra parameters per domain (2x model for ten domains)
models.architecture: ResNet28 plus per-domain 1x1 conv adapter (residual) and BN in each residual module
models.init_from: ImageNet-pretrained with adapters added, then shared weights frozen

other.domain predictor: light ResNet, three stacks of two residual units, half as deep

training.weight_decay: default 0.0005; adapters also 0.002 and 0.005, chosen per dataset by coarse grid search with cross-validation
training.regularisation: adapter shrinkage via weight decay (adapter tends to identity)

other.end-to-end variant: round-robin batch from each dataset, then a final pass on adapters

inference.samples: single run per cell; no seeds or error bars stated

other.domain label: given at test time except the dom-pred variant

metrics.name: Decathlon score S
metrics.definition: S = sum_d a_d max{0, Emax_d - E_d}^gamma_d, gamma=2, a_d=1000 (Emax_d)^-gamma so perfect = 1000 per domain; Emax = double the error of the fully fine-tuned network

eval.protocol: ImageNet pre-train then one domain at a time; single run, no significance test

availability.data: 'planning to make the data and an evaluation server public soon'

results.claim: Residual adapters with per-dataset weight decay reach higher mean accuracy than full fine-tuning at 2x parameters instead of 10x.
results.setup: ResNet28, ImageNet-primed, ten Visual Decathlon domains, one run
results.table: Table 1, row Res. adapt. decay, column mean (Finetune row: 76.51)

results.claim: Decathlon score of adapters with tuned decay exceeds fine-tuning (baseline 2500).
results.setup: same as above; Emax is double the fine-tuned error, so Finetune scores 2500 by construction
results.table: Table 1, row Res. adapt. decay, column S

results.claim: A single shared decay gives good mean accuracy but a low decathlon score because DTD and Flowers are poor.
results.setup: Res. adapt., default decay for all domains

results.claim: A 12x adapter model with a larger ResNet28 beats fine-tuning by about 600 decathlon points.
results.table: Table 1, row Res. adapt. (large), column S

results.claim: Fine-tuning only the last two conv layers (same parameter count) is much worse than adapters.
results.setup: twice the parameters of a vanilla ResNet, versus Res. adapt. with single decay
results.quote: This model obtains 64.7% mean accuracy over ten datasets
results.note: paper writes 73.9% here and 73.88% in Table 1

results.claim: Adapters without residual connection (low-rank filter parametrisation) are worse and converge slower.
results.quote: this approach achieves an accuracy of 70.3%

results.claim: Adapters add about 11% of parameters per domain.
Tuning only BN scale and bias lifts a frozen feature extractor on Aircraft.
results.setup: BN adapt. versus frozen features, under 0.1% domain-specific parameters

results.claim: Adapters keep ImageNet accuracy exactly while full fine-tuning forgets it.
results.metric: ImageNet accuracy after tuning on a target
results.setup: pairwise, each target task in turn; fine-tuning drops ImageNet to as low as 0.2 on Omniglot-like targets (see table)
results.table: Table 2, row Res. adapt. finetune all, column ImageNet (59.2)

results.claim: A small predictor identifies the domain with high accuracy and barely lowers the score.
results.setup: light ResNet domain classifier; S 2503 versus 2643

limits: Low resolution (64 px) lowers ImageNet and Flowers accuracy versus the state of the art.
Domain label is assumed at test time except in the domain-prediction variant.
No seeds, error bars or significance tests; the weight decay is chosen per dataset on validation.
Decathlon score depends on the fine-tuned baseline (Emax is double its error).
CNN only; a concurrent similar architecture (Rosenfeld & Tsotsos) is acknowledged.

terms.definition: g(x; alpha) = x + alpha * x, with alpha a bank of 1x1 filters; reduces to identity at zero coefficients
learning a single representation that works across several image domains, distinct from multiple-task learning

lineage.note: BN-only adaptation, special case of adapters
